title: Palette: A Modular and Efficient Framework for On-demand Authorized Safety Relaxation
claim: One-size-fits-all refusal fails professionals; authorized users should get domain-scoped relaxation, delivered through swappable provider-managed adapters.
layout: 3 role panels on top, deployment diagram below; check/cross response bars
description: The figure has two tiers. The top row has three rounded panels for a police officer, a vaccine scientist and a game developer. Each panel shows a persona icon and an 'Authorized scope' box that lists the allowed domain with a green check and the disallowed domains with a red cross. Under that, two example exchanges are stacked. A user icon asks an in-scope question in a labeled tag, such as Crime, Vaccine or Low-level violence, and a green-check bar with a colored robot replies 'Sure, I can help with that…'. The user then asks an out-of-scope question, and a red-tinted bar with a red robot replies 'I can't fulfill your request…'. The bottom panel is 'Provider-managed deployment'. A user marked 'Inference only' sends a prompt and receives a response from a 'Model + LoRA' server inside a dashed 'Backend' box labeled 'black box to users'. A provider icon sends an authorized profile and loads one of three colored LoRA modules: Crime in blue, Vaccine in green and Low-level violence in purple. The eye goes first to the red and green response bars.
caption: Illustration of the desired refusal relaxation for an authorized target domain.
abstract: Current safety alignment of foundation models largely follows a one-size-fits-all paradigm, applying the same refusal policy across users and contexts. As a result, models may refuse requests that are unsafe for general users but legitimate for authorized professionals, limiting helpfulness in specialized professional settings. Existing approaches either require costly realignment or rely on inference-time steering that suffers from imprecise control and added latency. To this end, we propose Palette, a modular, controllable, and efficient framework that selectively relaxes refusal behavior on authorized target domains while preserving standard safety elsewhere. Our method identifies a refusal direction via multi-objective search and internalizes it into the model through lightweight adaptation. Palette further supports modular composition: it learns domain-specific safety controls independently and composes them through parameter merging, enabling on-demand multi-domain authorization without retraining. Experiments across four safety benchmarks, multiple model variants, and both LLMs and VLMs show that Palette delivers precise safety control without sacrificing general utility, offering a practical path toward foundation models that adapt to diverse professional needs.
